response.sql: WITH acct AS (SELECT o.account_id AS account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM "order" o JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3), diffs AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM acct) AS diff FROM acct), reg AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff, AVG(diff) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_avg_diff FROM diffs) SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff, diff - region_avg_diff AS excess_over_region_avg FROM reg WHERE diff > region_avg_diff ORDER BY excess_over_region_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The account's region is taken from the account's own district (account.district_id -> district.A3), not from the client's district.
The overall average is the average of the per-account order counts across all account-region rows (not the average per order row).
Ties at the top 10 cutoff are broken arbitrarily since no secondary sort was specified.
